format.prompts: input: what upstream's session passed its prompt builder (extensionTools as their definitions give them). sections: the builder's sections in order; prompt: their text joined by blank lines.
format.discovery: files, dirs, cwd, trusted, flags: the tree and the command line. result: the custom prompt, the appended text, and the context files upstream's resource loader passes the builder.

placeholders.<tmp>: The case's temporary directory. The agent dir is <tmp>/agent; the working directory is below it.
placeholders.<bom>: A UTF-8 byte order mark (U+FEFF) at the start of a file to write.
placeholders.<product>: The product name in the prompt's first sentence (upstream: pi).

sections.name: preamble
sections.text: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside <product>, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

sections.name: tools
sections.text:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

sections.name: rules
sections.text:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

discovery.name: agent-dir-files
discovery.description: SYSTEM.md and APPEND_SYSTEM.md in the agent dir.

discovery.name: trusted-project-files-win
discovery.description: A trusted project's .pi files replace the agent dir's; same-named files are not combined.

discovery.name: untrusted-project-files-ignored
discovery.description: An untrusted project's .pi files are ignored.

discovery.name: each-file-resolves-alone
discovery.description: A project SYSTEM.md does not hide the agent dir's APPEND_SYSTEM.md.

discovery.name: project-dir-is-the-working-directory
discovery.description: Only the working directory's .pi is read, not an ancestor's.

discovery.name: flags-replace-discovered-files
discovery.description: --system-prompt and --append-system-prompt replace the discovered files; a flag naming a file reads it, without its byte order mark.

result.appendSystemPrompt:
flag append

extra from a file

discovery.name: one-flag-leaves-the-other-file
discovery.description: --append-system-prompt alone leaves the discovered SYSTEM.md in place.

discovery.name: byte-order-mark-and-empty-files
discovery.description: A byte order mark is dropped; an empty APPEND_SYSTEM.md appends nothing.

discovery.name: context-file-names
discovery.description: One context file per directory: AGENTS.override.md, then AGENTS.md, then CLAUDE.md. An override replaces only its own directory's file, and a directory with a context file's name is skipped.

discovery.name: working-directory-inside-the-agent-dir
discovery.description: The agent dir's context file is listed once when the agent dir is also an ancestor.

discovery.name: untrusted-project-keeps-context-files
discovery.description: Context files load whatever the trust decision.

discovery.name: no-context-files-flag
discovery.description: --no-context-files drops context files and keeps SYSTEM.md.

discovery.name: nested-worktree-shadows-main-checkout
discovery.description: A linked worktree inside its main checkout: the worktree's context file replaces the main checkout's same-named file. Other ancestors still load.

discovery.name: nested-worktree-with-another-file-name
discovery.description: The worktree's CLAUDE.md shadows only the main checkout's CLAUDE.md, so its AGENTS.md still loads.

discovery.name: sibling-worktree-shadows-nothing
discovery.description: A linked worktree beside its main checkout shadows nothing.
